subject: Post-call: regional performance constraints & action plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@novafintech.com>, Alex Shaw <alex.shaw@novafintech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: regional performance constraints & action plan

Hi Priya / Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. If I missed anything, flag it below.

Call highlights (from your requirements):
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end response <= 350ms for single-turn text gen in US/EU, <= 450ms in APAC (edge users).
- Throughput: steady-state 300 rps across US + EU, burst up to 600 rps for short windows; APAC steady 120 rps, burst 250 rps.
- Concurrency: average concurrent sessions ~40k (global), peak concurrency expected ~85k during promotions.
- Streaming: streaming responses are required for chat UX (token-by-token), with max-first-byte targets: 120ms in US/EU, 200ms APAC.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU at rest, APAC must route to customer-designated APAC region; logs can be aggregated but PII must be filtered prior to export.

Proposed next steps (action owners and timeline):
1) Fill the attached SLO worksheet with traffic distribution by region and expected token rates (Priya / Alex) — by 2027-04-18.
2) Redwood engineering to validate residency-routing plan and confirm Dedicated capacity / region residency options (Ben) — draft by 2027-04-20.
3) Network-trace sample from NovaFintech so we can validate tail latency at your edge (Alex) — by 2027-04-17.
4) Follow-up technical sync to lock down batching/quantization tradeoffs for APAC (30–45m) — propose times below.

Attachments: SLO-worksheet-NovaFintech.xlsx (worksheet template), sample-network-trace.txt (placeholder).

Scheduling: I have Tuesday 4/20 9–11am PT and Wednesday 4/21 1–3pm PT open — which works for you?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference for production
From: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@novafintech.com>

Cc: Alex Shaw <alex.shaw@novafintech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: regional performance constraints & action plan

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency numbers: the 350ms/450ms are for perceived latency (app to user) — our backend will accept up to an additional 100ms for Rdw inference; so your SLOs should be measured end-to-end from Redwood endpoint to our backend.
- Throughput: the 300 rps is for textual prompts at ~80 tokens per request (avg). During promotions we expect tokens/request to spike to ~300 tokens for long-form summarization jobs.
- Concurrency: 85k peak is global, but APAC accounts for ~20% of sessions and tends to have spiky auth patterns (short-lived bursts).
- Streaming: very important for our mobile chat clients; we need first token within 200ms in APAC and continuous streaming thereafter.
- Residency: confirmed — all customer content generated in EU must be persisted in EU GCP; APAC persistence must be in our APAC AWS account (we can provide KMS/key IDs).

I'll have the traffic breakdown and token-rate details in the SLO worksheet by EOD Sunday (4/18). I'll also upload a short network-trace (edge->origin) for your infra team.

One question for Ben/Marissa: do you have any recommended quantization profiles for APAC that balance peak throughput vs quality? We are sensitive to hallucinations on the summarization tasks.

Best,
Priya
Head of AI Product | NovaFintech

Attachment: will upload network-trace to the Drive link in Jordan's email.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Looping in Ben for the technical validation. Quick internal checklist before the sync:
- Identify Dedicated pool sizing to hit 300 rps / 600 burst (US/EU) and APAC pools for 120/250 burst. Include headroom for cache warming.
- Confirm streaming stack for APAC: edge gateways, local KV cache, and token flush strategy to meet first-byte targets.
- Data residency: confirm we can mount EU GCP buckets for persistence + customer KMS options. If NovaFintech provides KMS key IDs, we can integrate via our private deployment options.
- Ask cloudops partner (Enterprise Cloud) for circuit/peering checklist to reduce network tail latency — I’ll reach out.

Ben — can you do a quick feasibility estimate and notes by EOD Tuesday (4/20)? I can surface any gaps in the follow-up call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@novafintech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: regional performance constraints & action plan

Thanks — ran a quick pass on the numbers. Notes and open questions:

1) Sizing: to meet steady 300 rps (80 tokens avg) with 95th <=350ms we recommend a mixed approach: 3 dedicated US pools (zone-separated) + 2 EU pools sized for 150 rps each, APAC: 2 smaller pools in SYD + SIN with capacity for 150 rps combined and ability to scale to 250 rps with warm standby shards. Estimated GPU reserve: 22 x A100-equivalents (regionally split).

2) Streaming: to hit first-byte targets in APAC (<=200ms) we suggest colocated edge gateways in APAC POPs with prefix KV caching (hot prompts) and early-token prefetch heuristics. This reduces tail variance. Also recommend HTTP/2 streaming and TCP tuning for mobile clients.

3) Concurrency: 85k global peak is within planned autoscaler limits, but bursts with long-form tokens (300 tokens/request) will increase token-per-second consumption ~3–4x. We need to see the SLO worksheet to evaluate queueing/backpressure strategies.

4) Residency: we can mount EU GCP buckets and support bring-your-own-KMS. For APAC AWS persistence, we'll need the account IDs and cross-account role for write access; we can provide Terraform snippets.

Open questions for NovaFintech:
- Can you share representative payload sizes and attachments per request? (affects network egress and batching choices)
- Are promotions predictable windows or ad-hoc? Predictable windows let us pre-warm caches.

I'll attach a short feasibility PDF with the rough capacity numbers and the Terraform role template before the technical sync.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
